conservation.condition_narrative:
The painting is in good and stable condition as per its last examination in January, 2018. 
Surface cleaning and foamcore backing applied in 1983.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Williams College Museum of Art in 2025.
conservation.technical_description:
Support: 
The painting is fully housed, backed, and the frame is in good condition. 
Primary: 
The primary support consists of a medium weight plain weave linen canvas stretched onto a four-membered stretcher. There is a large canvas slub visible down the lower central quadrant of the painting. All keys are present and the canvas is stable. 
Ground and Paint: 
The paint medium is oil. There is good adhesion between the paint film and ground. There is microcissing in the dark green passages of paint which have been minimized with retouching (ground pigment and Soluvar) in 1983. 
Surface Coating: 
The painting was varnished in 1983 with Soluvar. The painting is evenly saturated.

cr_data.provenance:
Downtown Gallery, New York, 1947; to Kathryn Hurd (Mrs. Frank Hurd), 1948; to present collection, 1982. 
(Source: Williams College Museum of Art, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Miss O'Keeffe thinks painted about 1922." Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Exam. at Amer. Place, April 1946. . . . On backing: Initials in circle [not verified]. Note: O'Keeffe told me May 3, 1946 that she had just sold a Skunk Cabbage. It may be this one of possibly the 1923 'Skunk Cabbage.' She will give me the name of the owner. At Downtown Gal. 6/16/47." Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "O'Keeffe told me that later Cos Cob to State Department? Doris Bry 5/3/46"[see cat. no. 547]. Abiquiú Notebooks after 1977 indicates, "Bequest of Katherine Hurd, Williams College Museum of Art, Williamstown, Mass." Stretcher inscription 2 may indicate preparatory work. Reproduced in *The Sun* (December 1922). For a discussion of this series of paintings, see Charles Eldredge, "Skunk Cabbages, Seasons & Series," in *Georgia O'Keeffe: Natural Issues* 1918–1924(1992), pp. 26–43. See cat. nos. 1943, 1944. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
